rationale: A treats the problem as finding an Eulerian circuit. It checks the even-degree and connectivity conditions, then builds the chain with Hierholzer's algorithm, with clear comments and a small otherHalf helper. It runs in polynomial time and rejects impossible inputs immediately. B's backtracking is shorter and readable, but its worst-case time is exponential. It also tries every domino as the starting stone, although a closed chain can start anywhere. Its use of next = append(chain, ...) relies on subtle sharing of the slice's backing array between branches, which happens to be safe but is fragile. A's Hierholzer loop is a little clumsy because it rebuilds the incident-edge list at every step. Overall A is the more robust and better-founded design and stays clear.
